page.overview:
What is Elendilmir?

The Elendilmir, also known as the Star of Elendil, was the name given to the a star-shaped white gem set upon mithril fillets that existed in two forms after it was remade, thinking the original was lost. These great gems seemed to burn with an inner light. The second Elendilmir was borne as the token of royalty on the brows of the Kings of Arnor from Isildur's youngest son Valandil onwards. As such, the second was known by the names Star of the North and Star of the North Kingdom.

The first jewel dated back to the early centuries of Númenor, and belonged to Silmariën, the daughter of King Tar-Elendil. From her, it passed to her descendants the Lords of Andúnië. The gem was presumably made by elven smiths of the Undying Lands, but is not recounted.

Isildur had only been King for two years when he was waylaid by Orcs and lost in the Great River during the Disaster of the Gladden Fields. When he put on the One Ring to escape from the battle he became invisible but the Elendilmir did not, blazing instead like a red and wrathful star. Much later the Elendilmir was found by Saruman's trackers who had been sent to find the One Ring. They did not discover the Ring but they brought to him the Elendilmir and other things.

After the War of the Ring, King Elessar ordered the restoration of the Tower of Orthanc. During the restoration, a steel closet was found behind a hidden door by Gimli, in which was discovered a small golden tube without any inscription, containing the original Elendilmir. Elessar brought it back to Annúminas, but only wore it upon his brow during special occasions to risk no harm to it. During other occasions, he would wear the second Elendilmir that had descended to him.
